newsitem.title: USA: Russian assets top '96 emerging market chart--EMTA. [CORRECTED 23:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Russian assets top '96 emerging market chart--EMTA. [CORRECTED 23:15 GMT]

text.p: Russian Vnesheconombank loans dominated the top five slots in the performance of 84 emerging market assets in 1996, the Emerging Markets Traders Association (EMTA) said on Monday.

Russia's Vnesheconombank Yen loans topped the chart with a whopping 141.67 percent change in the average bid price. The price on these loans ended 1996 at 68-7/8 bid, up from 28-1/2 at the close of 1995, EMTA said.
Also exhibiting stellar performances in 1996 were assets (corrects from loans) from the Ivory Coast, Ecuador and Venezuela, it said.
But assets (corrects from loans) from Cuba, Bulgaria and Brazil ranked among the worst performers.
EMTA based their figures on the changes in price on Brady Bond and restructured loan assets as reported by 15 major dealers in the emerging markets industry.

Institutions participating in EMTA's project included Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Limited plc, Bank of America, Bear Stearns & Co, Chase Manhattan Corp, Citicorp Securities, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Indosuez Capital, ING Barings, Goldman Sachs & Co, J.P. Morgan, Merrill Lynch & Co, Paribas Capital Markets, Salomon Brothers Inc, Santander Investment and Swiss Bank Corp.
